scope: Bounded source and raw-byte review of four representative SerializedExpressionNodeGraph resources among the 22 captured weapon-core resources. Samples: smallest M1014 PresEx, SharedSoldierAbilityWeapon, M45A1 Blacklight SimEx, and M2010 ESR PresEx.

capture.all22CaptureFacts: The existing capture manifest records 22/22 successful SerializedExpressionNodeGraph bodies, type ID 7dd4cc89, 367552 bytes total. This review directly inspected four representative bodies only.

files.finding: ResourceType enum includes SerializedExpressionNodeGraph = 0x7DD4CC89. ResAssetEntry stores ResRid, ResType, and ResMeta as separate resource-entry properties.
ReadResourceRef reads a UInt64 and wraps it in ResourceRef. The reader has generic resource references, not a graph-payload decoder.

RIFF EBX parsing records resource-reference fixup offsets. EBXX parsing reads array and boxed-value tables. Boxed records contain offset/count/hash/type/classRef fields; the code does not associate these EBX/EBXX records with byte sections of a RES payload.
Resource stream retrieval is handled by the asset/resource manager; the inspected code did not dispatch a SerializedExpressionNodeGraph body to a typed parser.

sourceEvidence.searchResult: A bounded text-source search of the local Frosty SDK/plugin tree found the exact type name in the ResourceType enum and generated game string tables. No graph-body parser or format definition was located in the inspected source. Binary strings were not treated as implementation evidence.

observedByteFacts: All four bodies begin with 16 zero bytes. Their separate captured 16-byte resource metadata fields are also all zero.
All four file lengths are multiples of 16 (128, 816, 1344, 1792). This is a size observation only; it does not establish alignment rules or section boundaries.
At byte offset 0x20, the little-endian 32-bit value is 0x20 in M1014 and 0x30 in the other three samples. The value's meaning is unknown.
The remaining body bytes vary. No authoritative field map or section split can be assigned from these four samples alone.

hypotheses.initial: The type name SerializedExpressionNodeGraph and resource names suggest that these bodies may encode expression graphs. This is a naming-based hypothesis only.
hypotheses.not_established: No opcode, node name, field interpretation, runtime equation, or relationship between resource payload offsets and EBX/EBXX metadata is established by this review.

conclusion: The local SDK substantiates the resource type code and generic resource-ID handling, but not the inner SerializedExpressionNodeGraph format. EBX resource-reference fixups and EBXX array/boxed-value tables are parsed as EBX metadata; inspected source does not connect them to sections within these RES bodies. Repeated raw prefixes and 16-byte-multiple sizes are observations, not a decoded layout. A useful typed decode is blocked pending an authoritative graph reader/specification or independent format evidence that maps boundaries and fields.
